notes.note: Reading 1 chosen (operands shall be values unless the operator clause allows templates); test uses a template as operand of '+', which no clause allows.

Reading 1 chosen: each type uses the notation allowed for it (assignment and list for record, assignment for set/union/anytype, list for record of/set of/array). Titan warning is wrong: Titan requires a non-standard 'extension "anytype ..."' attribute to give anytype fields; per clause 6.2.6 anytype contains all known types.

Every non-equality operator also has type restrictions, so a violation cannot be fully isolated; test uses 'type integer address' so that null is a valid value of the left operand's type and '<' accepts the integer root type.

Not observable: presence checking operators yield boolean while unary +/- require integer/float, so no well-typed expression distinguishes their precedence. Test only combines both operator kinds in one expression.

Not observable: shift/rotate operands are strings/lists while relational operators need integer/float/enumerated, so no well-typed expression without conversions distinguishes their precedence. Test combines shifts/rotates and relational operators via bit2int.
